## Relevant Symbols
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:660`: the claim records `--pid "$$"`. The lease heartbeat (`:688`) loops while `$$` or
  the worker lives, so whichever process runs these lines must be the one that survives.
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:684–691`: the worker is started with `&` as the launcher's child and awaited. Both are
  in the caller's process group and cgroup today, which is the root cause of the item.
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:690`: trap on TERM/INT/HUP kills the worker and records exit 143.
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:110`: `LANE_MODE=1` iff `HEFESTO_TRUSTED_TOP` is set. Existing checks "stand down" in a
  terminal or the smoke suite, and that is the precedent for the `/proc` and detach test seams.
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:214`: the run mode refuses inside a sandbox, so the launcher always runs unsandboxed and
  `systemd-run --user` can reach the user bus.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:461–462`: `max_builders` validated with `^[1-8]$`, the pattern for `max_concurrent_runs`.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:464–469`: the busy computation with `JQ_LIVE_OWNER` over `"$DIR"/*.json`. Verify is exempt from
  the stage limit only.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:442`: no `--pid` means interactive. So "a run" is exactly an owner with `.owner.pid`.
- `hooks/ledger-lanes.sh:167`: a lease older than 5 min is stale. A detached run keeps renewing because its
  heartbeat runs inside the detached process.
- `hooks/quality-before-commit.sh:133–139`: shellcheck exit 1 is a finding; any other code is an advisory ("could not
  check — out of memory?"), added after a 137 on `tests/smoke.sh` on 2026-10-23.
- `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:285`: `echo "setup: note: …"` inside `--check` does not change the result. That is the
  model for the oomd note.

## Existing Patterns & Conventions
- Refusals: `die "<cmd> <id>: <value> — <expected shape / remedy>"` to stderr, non-zero (`session-launch.sh:46`,
  `ledger.sh:462`).
- Config: `cfg '.orchestrate.<key> // <default>'` (`session-launch.sh:176`), `cfgp` in ledger (`ledger.sh:461`).
- Sourced libs live beside the hooks with `# shellcheck shell=bash` and are sourced via `$HERE`
  (`session-launch.sh:50–52`, `hooks/launch-item.sh:1`).
- Smoke parts for new features are separate files sourced at the end of `tests/smoke.sh` (`:6794–6803`). Mutations
  are `sed` on a copy plus `cmp -s` to prove the mutation applied (`tests/smoke.sh:1374`).
- Fake binaries are written into a temp `bin` dir prepended to PATH (`tests/smoke.sh:1368`, `:2252`).
- Zero-install (constitution 4): bash, jq, git, awk, coreutils. `systemd-run`/`setsid` are optional host tools and
  are detected, never required.

## Open Questions
- None blocking. Risk carried into the plan: shellcheck is a GHC binary, and its runtime reserves a large virtual
  address range at start. Under `ulimit -v 2097152` it may fail to start, not just fail on large files. Probing this
  here was blocked by the session's permission surface (no approval available), so implementation must measure it
  first (Plan, Risk R1).
